about-title: Public information should be easier to use
about-lede: BetterMati.org makes public information about the City of Mati, Davao Oriental easier to find, understand and verify.
about-note: A volunteer-run civic portal that organizes city services, government information, public funds and official-source data in one place.
about-flow-label: How BetterMati turns official sources into clearer public information
about-flow-origin-detail: Charters · Reports · Census data · Public records
about-flow-result-detail: Searchable · Structured · Linked to its source
about-why-title: Public information shouldn’t be hard to find just because it lives in different places
about-why-p1: Information about a city is spread across many places: charters and department pages, financial reports, census tables, council records, social media posts and PDF files. To find one answer, residents often need to know which office publishes it first.
about-why-p2: BetterMati brings those sources into one resident-facing structure while keeping the original source visible, so residents, students, researchers and civil society can find what they need without first learning how the City Government is organized.
about-why-goal: The goal is not to replace official sources. It is to make them easier to find, understand and check.
about-sources-title: Public information lives across many sources
about-dir-lede: Published public information, structured into six directories:
about-dir-services: Service guidance by category, with responsible offices and the sources behind each guide.
about-dir-government: Elected officials, City offices, barangays and official contact channels.
about-dir-legislation: How ordinances and resolutions move through the Sangguniang Panlungsod, with published records.
about-dir-transparency: City receipts and spending from DBM fiscal records.
about-dir-statistics: Population, barangays, income class and poverty estimates with their sources.
about-dir-visit: Places to see in Mati, the seasons and how to plan a trip.
about-today-note: Each collection has its own unit, coverage and reference period, so these figures shouldn’t be added together. They describe what BetterMati currently publishes, not every City dataset or record. If something isn’t on BetterMati, that doesn’t mean the record, office, service or document doesn’t exist.
about-process-title: From official source to usable civic information
about-process-lede: How information moves from a public source to a BetterMati page:
about-step-find-desc: An official public page, document, dataset or other attributable source.
about-step-check-desc: Who published it, when, and what it actually supports.
about-step-structure-desc: Organize the facts for residents without changing what the source says.
about-step-publish-desc: Show the source, its scope, the date it was checked and its limits.
about-principle-source-desc: Published facts stay connected to the public source they came from.
about-principle-scope-desc: A dataset is presented as what it covers, not as something broader.
about-principle-unknown-desc: Missing or unconfirmed information is marked, not guessed. That’s why many fees and contacts say “Confirm with office”.
about-principle-residents-desc: Information is organized around what people are trying to find or do.
about-we-do-organize: Organize public information from official sources
about-we-do-links: Keep source links and checked dates visible
about-we-do-independent: Run an independent, volunteer-built civic portal
about-we-dont-replace: Replace the official City Government website
about-we-dont-speak: Speak on behalf of the City Government
about-we-dont-alter: Create or change official government records
about-we-dont-infer: Fill in facts a source doesn’t support
about-we-dont-transact: Process applications, payments, complaints or emergency requests
about-trust-title: Built to be checked, not taken on authority
about-evidence-body: Wherever the public record allows, BetterMati keeps the path from a published fact back to its original source visible.
about-evidence-funds: City receipts and spending, with the DBM record behind them.
about-evidence-stats: Population and poverty figures, with their PSA sources.
about-evidence-services: Every service page lists the sources behind its guidance.
about-independent-official: Not an official City Government website
about-independent-official-desc: BetterMati.org is a volunteer-run initiative. It is not run by the City Government of Mati and does not replace official government channels.
about-independent-attribution: Source links are attribution, not endorsement
about-independent-attribution-desc: A link to an official source shows where information came from. It does not mean the government endorses or authored BetterMati.
about-independent-original: Use original sources for important decisions
about-independent-original-desc: For legal, administrative or financial decisions, check the linked original source or ask the responsible office.
about-open-title: Open, volunteer-built and free to use
about-open-body: BetterMati.org costs the people of Mati nothing. Its code is public on GitHub, and designers, developers, writers and translators are all welcome to help.

trans-description: City of Mati’s FY2025 reported finances, 2026–2027 planning figures and selected procurement records, with official sources.
trans-units: Amounts in millions of Philippine pesos (M)
trans-finance-note: FY2025 reported figures are from DBM BESF 2027, Table F.13. External receipts include NTA; non-income receipts include borrowing. SEF is the Special Education Fund. Non-operating expenditures include capital outlay and principal debt payments. These financial flows are not the approved annual budget.
trans-cash-note: Ending cash is shown after prior-year payable payments and continuing appropriations. It is not simply receipts minus expenditures. Amounts retain the source’s rounding to two decimal places.
trans-procurement-note: These notices are a selected sample, not a complete inventory. The Approved Budget for the Contract (ABC) is the bidding ceiling, not the awarded price or money already spent. National and city procurements are identified separately and are not added to the city’s annual figures.
trans-project-unknowns: Contractor, award amount and physical completion have not been verified from this notice. A procurement status does not prove delivery or completion.
trans-project-11374254: Level II potable water supply system in Barangay Badas
trans-project-11439666: Completion works for the cultural and sports center in Dahican
trans-method: Checked on 24 September 2026. Financial figures are transcribed from Mati’s rows in DBM BESF 2027, Tables F.13–F.15 (PDF pages 3–4), published 11 August 2026. Footnotes credit DOF-BLGF/LIFT submissions. Procurement citations link to DA FFEDIS and PhilGEPS.
trans-gaps: Quarterly breakdowns and completed FY2026 actuals remain unverified. The PDF text layer has inconsistent continuation-year headings; DBM’s index and the visible table titles identify 2025, 2026 and 2027. Missing records do not mean zero spending. The 2025 opening cash differs from the previous release’s 2024 closing cash; no year-to-year cash reconciliation is claimed.
trans-audit-note: This compilation does not assess audit compliance. The COA report directory is provided for further research; a Mati audit report was not retrieved during this check.
stats-verified-intro: Population, city finances, and poverty estimates for Mati, with source links and reference years.
stats-checked-on: Sources checked: {{date}}. Each figure uses the latest reference period verified for that indicator.
stats-finance-period: FY2025 actual receipts, published in DBM BESF 2027 on 11 August 2026. Based on local treasurers’ LIFT submissions to DOF-BLGF.
stats-receipts-note: Total receipts include non-income receipts such as borrowings. NTA is already included in external sources. These are reported receipts, not the approved budget or a COA audit opinion.
stats-poverty-definition: Estimated share of Mati’s population with income below the poverty threshold. PSA small area estimates, with 90% confidence intervals.
stats-poverty-release: Reference years: 2018, 2021 and 2023. Released 6 February 2026. Values were checked in an archived copy of PSA’s workbook (Mati, PSGC 112509); the direct PSA download was unavailable during this review.
stats-economic-unverified: City-level business counts, agricultural land, employment rates and sector shares have not been verified in a dated official source. Previously displayed figures are withheld. Provincial or regional rates are not substituted for Mati data.
stats-cmci-unverified: Mati’s recent CMCI scores and rankings could not be verified because the DTI profile was inaccessible. Previously displayed scores, trends and indicator bars are withheld pending verification. Rankings must identify their city category.
trans-outlook-note: These amounts are published in DBM’s BESF 2027. We classify them as planning figures because the publication predates the end of 2026 and all of 2027. The tables reuse actual-data footnotes without separately explaining estimates. They are not verified full-year actuals or evidence of an enacted city budget. Amounts are in PHP millions; NTA is included in receipts.
trans-project-1713: Rice assistance for indigent individuals or families
leg-records-scope: Selected references, not a complete register. No 2025–2026 records have been verified for this collection. This does not mean no measures were passed.
leg-records-evidence: Government reporting identifies the numbers and subjects below. Summaries are not official titles. Signed texts, session dates, amendments and current legal status remain unverified.
leg-record-abunda: Establishment of the Abunda Festival to recognize farmers, fisherfolk and livestock raisers.
leg-record-meat: Ordinance cited by the city veterinarian in enforcement against undocumented processed meat products. The report does not supply its official title.
leg-record-eagle: Establishment of a 7,000-hectare Philippine Eagle Sanctuary, as reported by PNA. Issued by Mati’s former municipal council.
leg-legal-source: Legal basis: Republic Act No. 9408, sections 17–21
leg-budget-rule: Appropriations require an ordinance or law; a resolution alone does not replace an appropriations ordinance.
leg-copy-heading: How to verify the full record
leg-copy-body: Request a certified copy from the Secretary to the Sangguniang Panlungsod of Mati. Include the measure’s number and year; ask for the signed text, passage date, amendments and posting or publication record. Fees prescribed by ordinance may apply.
leg-copy-source: RA 9408: duties of the Secretary to the Sangguniang Panlungsod
leg-archive-unavailable: The previously linked Mati council archive could not be retrieved during this review (24 September 2026).
rising-preview-note: Projects with published sources. Statuses reflect the dated records, not live construction updates.
rising-note: Selected projects in Mati with source links and dated evidence. Bidding ceilings, appropriations, announced funding and reported costs mean different things; these amounts are not added to the city’s annual spending. This is not a complete inventory.
rising-airport-detail: The 2026 national budget lists ₱700 million for Mati Airport under DOTr. This is an appropriation, not a contract award or actual expenditure. This budget document does not establish construction progress or an opening date.
rising-macambol-detail: PNA reports Hallmark Mining Corp.’s statement that the Silad–Banluton water system was completed and serves about 250 households. Funded through the company’s Social Development and Management Program (SDMP); not city expenditure. No independent completion certificate was reviewed.
rising-fishport-detail: A February 2023 PNA report quotes the city’s announcement of ₱150 million in additional funding for Phase 2. The announcement does not establish the contract price, actual spending or present completion.
rising-coastal: Fish port access road and coastal highway
rising-coastal-detail: The city announced ₱2 billion for a 2.25-kilometre route linking Mati Park and Baywalk, the fish port and Sitio Bilawan in February 2023, with DPWH coordination. Current construction progress is unverified. This does not confirm the former “Baywalk & Boulevard Extension” listing.
rising-procurement-detail: The PhilGEPS notice is marked Awarded. Its ABC is a bidding ceiling, not the awarded amount. Physical completion and current operation have not been verified.

a11y-page-lede: BetterMati.org aims to make public information about the City of Mati usable by as many people as possible, including people who use screen readers, navigate by keyboard, or browse on a phone over a slow connection.
a11y-page-standard-body: We use WCAG 2.1 Level AA as our working accessibility goal. This statement is not a formal certification or the result of a third-party audit.
a11y-page-approach-standard: WCAG 2.1 Level AA is the goal we design and review against. Changes are checked with automated audits (Lighthouse) and by hand with a keyboard and at phone widths before they ship.
a11y-page-approach-means: No independent accessibility audit has been done yet, so some pages may not meet every success criterion. When we find a gap, we treat it as a bug to fix, not a known exception.
a11y-page-measure-semantic-desc: Pages use header, navigation, main and footer landmarks, and headings follow the visible order of the content, so screen-reader users can move around by structure.
a11y-page-measure-keyboard-desc: Links, buttons, menus and search fields can be reached and used with a keyboard, and every focusable element shows a visible focus outline.
a11y-page-measure-alt-desc: Meaningful images carry descriptive alternative text. Decorative icons are hidden from assistive technology so they are not read aloud.
a11y-page-measure-contrast-desc: Body text, links and secondary text use colours chosen to meet the WCAG AA contrast ratio of at least 4.5:1 against their background.
a11y-page-measure-motion-desc: If your device is set to reduce motion, sliding and scaling animations are switched off and content simply fades in.
a11y-page-measure-languages-desc: The site can be switched between English and Cebuano, and the page language changes with it so screen readers use the right pronunciation.
a11y-page-limit-pdf-desc: Some linked documents, such as the City's Citizen's Charter, are PDFs published by the City Government and may not be tagged for screen readers.
a11y-page-limit-external-desc: Links to official government portals and other external services lead to sites we do not control, which may not behave the same way as this one.
a11y-page-limit-translations-desc: The Cebuano translation is still a small starter set, so many pages fall back to English until a full translation is reviewed.
a11y-page-limits-note: If part of the site is hard to use with assistive technology, telling us which page and what happened helps us find where to improve.
a11y-page-feedback-text: Tell us what you were trying to do, which page the problem happened on, and the browser or assistive technology you were using.
